questions.question: CARVER ROBOWELD LIMITED owes 1.48 rupees of loans for every rupee of its owners' money. Which is closest to the truth?

choices.text: Its loans are small to manageable next to what the owners have put in.
Its loans are heavy: lenders have more riding on it than its owners.
Loans never matter for a company that makes a profit.

questions.explanation: At 1.48 rupees of loans per rupee of owners' money, lenders have more riding on CARVER ROBOWELD LIMITED than its owners, and repayments are due even in bad years.

questions.question: An unofficial grey market premium of ₹5 a share is being quoted. How much should you rely on it?

choices.text: Completely: it tells you the listing price.
A little at most: it is unregulated and easy to push around.
It is set by the stock exchange.

questions.explanation: The grey market premium of ₹5 for CARVER ROBOWELD LIMITED is gossip with a number on it: nobody regulates it, and it often turns out wrong.
